description_full: Fiverr International Ltd. operates an online marketplace worldwide. The company's platform enables sellers to sell their services and buyers to buy them. Its platform offers digital services, including logo design and blog post writing, video creation, website development, and social media marketing services. The company also provides value added services comprising Fiverr Ads, an advertising tool that allows sellers to promote services on platform; Seller Plus, a subscription program that equips sellers with tools, such as advanced analytics and marketing capabilities; AutoDS, an end-to-end dropshipping automation tool that allows customers to track orders across channels; and financial tools, including faster withdrawal, local currency payout, and cash advance for sellers, as well as software talent platform. It serves businesses of various sizes, as well as sellers comprising a group of freelancers and agencies. Fiverr International Ltd. was incorporated in 2010 and is headquartered in Tel Aviv-Yafo, Israel.

financial_summary: Fiverr International Ltd. is a micro-cap communication services business with a $289M market cap on $431M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +8% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are expanding by +5.4pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at -26% against a 11% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 82% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $104M in free cash flow — roughly 24 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 4.98× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin -0.6× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 11.2% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and stock-based comp at 12% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insiders hold 14% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.0× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
